description: Reusable, parametric design rules from the 246 South 2nd Street model. Values match DEFAULT_RULES in index.html; a new building model can start from this file.

sideOffset.label: Separation from east and west (side) lot lines
sideOffset.ratioMeaning: Offset = building height above grade / ratio (same units). 600 = 1 in per 50 ft of height.
sideOffset.roundMeaning: Round the offset up to the next multiple of roundIn inches.
sideOffset.appliesTo: Lot lines not on a street (side lot lines). Rear and street lot lines are not offset in this model.
sideOffset.source: NYC Building Code 2022 §1613.4 (structural separations). A smaller gap is allowed by rational analysis, never under 1 in.
sideOffset.example: 85 ft tall: 85 / 50 = 1.7 in, rounded up to 2 in

amenityCap.label: Amenity deduction cap
amenityCap.meaning: Amenity space is deducted up to this % of residential floor area.
amenityCap.source: Project assumption from the original model, confirm with the zoning analysis
amenityCap.basis: 5% of the building's residential floor area, market-rate and affordable together, before the amenity itself is deducted (ZR 23-231). The amenity must be enclosed floor area on a floor that has floor area; amenity drawn on an open level deducts nothing.
amenityCap.thisBuilding: 3rd floor amenity room at the street, 32'-6" x 13'-11" = 452 SF, sized to the cap so it is fully deducted; reached from the elevator landing.

wallExcl.label: Qualifying exterior wall thickness exclusion
wallExcl.meaning: For existing-building projects only: wall thickness added to a building existing on 12/6/2023 (over-cladding with R-1.5 per inch, or re-cladding meeting the current energy code envelope requirements), up to 12 in, or walls built between 4/30/2012 and 12/6/2023 that met the old Zone Green rule, is left out of floor area. Off for 246 South 2nd Street, a new building.
wallExcl.condition: Not available to new buildings since City of Yes for Carbon Neutrality (12/6/2023); new buildings use the 5% ultra low energy building exclusion instead. The old 8 in / U-factor test applied to walls built 2012-2023.
wallExcl.source: ZR 12-10 definitions of floor area (exclusion 12) and qualifying exterior wall thickness, as amended 12/6/2023

mechanicalClosets.label: In-unit mechanical closets
mechanicalClosets.meaning: Each unit gets a mechanical closet of about 40 SF (30 SF in a studio) holding a ducted heat-pump air handler, an ERV and a heat-pump water heater, with the code service clearance in front. Deducted 100% as accessory mechanical equipment space.
mechanicalClosets.limit: ZR 12-10 excludes floor space for accessory mechanical equipment plus the minimum space needed for maintenance and access. There is no square-foot cap in R6 (the caps are only in R1-2A to R5), but DOB only allows space that actually holds equipment and its required clearance, so the equipment schedule has to back up the size.
mechanicalClosets.source: ZR 12-10 floor area exclusions; NYC Mechanical Code access and working space; confirm with the MEP engineer

zoneGreen.label: Zone Green deduction
zoneGreen.meaning: When on for a building, deduct this % of the zoning floor area above grade (residential plus commercial, before this exclusion), taken off the residential floor area (capped at the residential floor area). Shown as a bonus on the market-rate residential allowance.
zoneGreen.source: ZR 12-10 (City of Yes for Carbon Neutrality) excludes 5% of the floor area of a qualifying building; project owner set the base as the zoning floor area above grade. Confirm with the zoning analysis
zoneGreen.condition: Only for a fully electrified building (an existing building brought to Local Law 154) or an ultra low energy building. A new building qualifies only as an ultra low energy building: all-electric (LL154) and, above three stories, an energy use intensity about 50% or more below a reference building (Passive House level). Confirm the exact threshold and documentation with the energy consultant; without it the 5% is lost.

deductions.label: Floor area deductions, % of each area deducted
deductions.source: Project assumption from the original model, confirm with the zoning analysis

core.label: Elevator and stair core
core.meaning: One core stacked on every floor, sized from the stair rule. Width (outside) = core wall + stair + wall between + stair + core wall. Length = stair end wall + that floor's stair length + divider wall + elevator shaft + elevator end wall. The long walls and the elevator stay put on every floor, so only taller floors get a longer core. Counts as floor area on every floor; on commercial floors it counts as residential unless switched off for that floor.
core.thisBuilding: Against the east exterior wall, which serves as its long east side; 6 in core walls on the other sides; stair 7'-8" clear; 6'-0" elevator on the street side. Length follows each floor's height.
core.attachMeaning: The core can use an exterior wall as one long side: it has no wall of its own there, and the stair's clear width is measured from the exterior wall's inside face.
core.countsEveryStory: The core (stairs and elevator shaft) is floor area on every story it passes through, including a story with no other enclosed space; the model counts any part of it outside the drawn outline.

cellar.label: Cellar
cellar.source: Project assumption from the original model, confirm with the zoning analysis

stair.label: Scissor stair (two interlocking exit stairs in one enclosure)
stair.formula: risers = ceil(floor height / max riser); flights = ceil(floor height / 12 ft); treads = risers - flights; stair length = treads x tread + (flights + 1) x landing; landing = min(stair width, 48 in); stairs width = 2 x stair width + wall between
stair.thisBuilding: Stairs 7'-8" wide inside (44 + 4 + 44 in); 22'-11" long for 10 ft floors, 23'-10" for 11 ft, 25'-8" for 12 ft, 31'-2" for the 14 ft 1st floor
stair.notes: 36 in stairs are allowed if the stair serves only Group R-2, the building is 125 ft or less and the stair serves 30 or fewer occupants per floor (1011.2 exc. 1.2), or 50 or fewer occupants in total (exc. 1.1). In R-2, scissor stairs can count as two exits when enclosed and separated by 2-hour masonry and the exit doors are at least 15 ft apart (1007.1.1 exc. 3). A 4 in wall between the stairs may not give the 2-hour masonry separation that exception needs; confirm with the architect.

units.label: Units (condo) and how they are measured
units.meaning: A unit is a record (number, tenure, bedrooms, bathrooms, extra rooms, AMI for affordable, notes) with one drawn part on each floor it occupies, so duplexes and penthouses span floors. Sellable SF is drawn to the outside face of exterior walls and the centerline of demising and corridor walls (offering plan convention), less any light well. Interior SF subtracts the walls inside it (approximate). Terraces tied to a unit are its private outdoor space. Exposure comes from which unit edges face the street, the rear, the light well or a side yard.
units.checks: Affordable units: interior SF at least minSF for the bedroom count. Residential units: at least one street or rear exposure, since the light well cannot provide legally required windows.
units.numbering: New units are numbered by floor and letter (3A, 3B ...); copying a floor makes new units with that floor's numbers.
units.source: Project owner: offering plan measurement, units can span floors; minimum sizes from the HPD design guidelines, confirm

rooms.label: Habitable rooms and windows
rooms.meaning: Each unit has one living room of at least 150 SF; other habitable rooms (bedrooms) at least 80 SF with no side under 8 ft. Every habitable room needs a window onto a legal open space (the street, the rear yard or a terrace on our lot), with glass of at least 10% of its floor area. Windows on the light well give light but are not legally required windows (it is sized as a court without required windows); windows are not allowed in lot line walls. Dens, baths, closets and kitchens in an open plan do not need windows.
rooms.openings: Windows default to 5'-0" wide, sill 2'-6", head 8'-0"; doors 2'-8" (baths and closets 2'-6"), entry doors 3'-0", sliding doors 6'-0", heads 7'-0" (sliders 8'-0").
rooms.thisBuilding: All residential floors laid out (2026-10-19). 4F affordable 1BR + den and 4R 1BR + den; 5F/6F 2BR/2BA with bedroom 2 on the light well (flagged: not a legal window) and 5R/6R 1BR + den; 7F studio with the dormer (window on the street, sliding door to the setback terrace) and 7R 1BR + den; PH 1BR/1.5BA: primary suite at the rear, living at the street, private U-stair to the roof. Roof: lounge, dining, sun deck, outdoor kitchen, screened heat pump condensers, private stair bulkhead.
rooms.source: NYC Multiple Dwelling Law 30-31, Housing Maintenance Code, BC 1205 and 1208, BC 705.8; confirm with the architect
rooms.fixtures: Each living / dining / kitchen is laid out with a kitchen counter (25 in deep) and island, a dining table, a sofa and coffee table: kitchen on the inside wall, living at the windows.
rooms.lotLineWindows: Lot line windows are allowed where the owner chooses (7th and 8th floors on the west wall, above #242's roof, about 62 ft). They need protected (fire-rated) openings under the Building Code's exterior wall rules and usually a light and air easement; they add light but never count as legally required windows. Baths get a 4'-6" sill.
rooms.wetFixtures: Baths: tub (5'-0" x 2'-6") across the end away from the door, or a 3'-0" shower where the bath is under 5 ft wide; toilet (1'-9" x 2'-5") and vanity (2'-6" x 1'-9") along the wall away from the door, wrapping to the opposite wall when the room is short, keeping an 18 in aisle. Powder rooms: toilet and vanity. Laundry: stacked W/D 2'-6" square in the far corner. Mechanical closets: air handler 2'-6" square, heat pump water heater 2'-0" square and ERV along the back wall, with the service space in front kept clear (the ERV goes overhead where the closet is too short).

roof.label: Roof level
roof.meaning: A roof level sits over the top floor. Its outline (the top floor's footprint) is private outdoor space, not floor area, and it does not add to the building height. The core continues as a bulkhead: the elevator overruns without a stop at the roof, and the stair reaches the roof.
roof.notes: Elevator and stair bulkheads are permitted obstructions above the height limit within limits (ZR 23-62); NYC BC 1011.12 generally needs a stair to the roof on buildings four or more stories, so confirm how a private roof squares with roof access for the other units and the FDNY.
roof.source: Project owner: private roof, elevator goes up but does not open; confirm with the architect

stairBlock.label: Placed stairs (Block > Stairs)
stairBlock.kinds: straight (one flight, direct), straight2 (two flights in line with a landing), l (L-shaped, corner landing), u (U-shaped switchback, full-width turn landing), scissor (two interlocking stairs), helical (feature stair: treads fanned around an open well, tread depth measured on the walking line 12 in out from the well; stacked blocks continue from where the lower one ends)
stairBlock.meaning: A stair placed on a floor rises from that floor to the floor above, using the stair rule (max riser, tread, landing, max 12 ft per flight). The stair from the cellar to the 1st floor is a direct straight run, not a scissor stair. Each flight defaults to the stair rule width; under 36 in is flagged.
stairBlock.sizing: risers = ceil(floor height / max riser); straight: treads = risers - 1, length = treads x tread + 2 landings; two-flight types split the risers evenly, each flight has risers - 1 treads; landing = min(width, 48 in); turn landings are as deep as the stair is wide
stairBlock.thisBuilding: Cellar (12 ft) to 1st floor: straight run, 21 risers at 6.86 in, 20 treads at 11 in, 25'-8" x 3'-8" at 44 in wide including a landing at each end
stairBlock.source: NYC Building Code 2022 §1011.2, 1011.5.2, 1011.6, 1011.8; project owner: direct stair from the cellar

helical.meaning: Default open well 6 ft across; width per the stair rule (44 in), so about 13'-4" across overall. A convenience stair, not an exit stair: spiral and curved stairs count toward egress only in limited cases (BC 1011.9, 1011.10), and an open stair through three levels needs the floor openings protected (BC 1019 / 712): confirm with the architect.
helical.thisBuilding: Feature stair at 40 ft from the rear, centered across the lot: cellar to 1st (21 risers, 263 degrees) and 1st to 2nd (24 risers, 302 degrees), continuous.

court.label: Light well (small inner court with no legally required windows facing it)
court.meaning: Dimensions are the clear open court, measured to the court walls and the lot line; walls are outside it. Portions at or below 75 ft: at least 200 SF and no dimension under 10 ft. Above 75 ft: 300 SF and 15 ft. A court on a side lot line is an inner court. Not floor area.
court.sizing: depth = minimum dimension; length = max(minimum dimension, minimum area / depth)
court.thisBuilding: West lot line (top edge of the plan), from the 4th floor to the roof, 20'-0" x 10'-0" (200 SF) on floors 4-8. The 1st floor is 13'-11" so the 8th floor level is 74'-11", just below 75 ft.
court.measureMeaning: Which height decides the 75 ft threshold: 'top' of each story (stricter, the default) or the story's 'floor' level. This building uses 'floor'; a plan examiner may read the rule as the top of the story, which would put the whole 8th floor above 75 ft.
court.walls: Light well clear size is measured to its walls and the lot line; its walls sit outside the clear area. When moved along the building its edges snap to wall faces, the core and area corners.
court.skylightBelow: Where the light well lands on a terrace (the 2nd floor roof, 3rd floor level), put a skylight the size of the light well (20'-0" x 8'-10" inside the walls) so its daylight reaches the floor below (the 2nd floor library). It is a walk-on or guarded unit in the terrace deck and adds no floor area.

corridorDeduction.label: Corridor floor area exclusion
corridorDeduction.meaning: 50% when the corridor has at least 20 SF of glazing (directly in the corridor, in an adjacent stair enclosure wall with a door having at least 16 SF of glazing, or in common space along the corridor); plus 50% when the corridor is no more than 100 ft from the vertical circulation core to the farthest dwelling unit door. Together: 100%.

useAreas.label: Residential and Commercial areas
useAreas.meaning: Drawn inside the gross outline to set the use of that part of a floor (for example a residential lobby on a commercial floor). The rest of the floor follows the floor's use. Deductions and amenity count toward the use of the area they sit in. The core is not double counted when it sits inside a Residential area.

sellable.label: Sellable area: residential free-market, residential affordable, commercial
sellable.meaning: Tracked for efficiency only and not part of the floor area math. Shown as FM / A / C in the table. Residential efficiency = (free-market + affordable sellable) / residential gross, above grade.

extWall.label: Exterior walls
extWall.meaning: Exterior walls sit inside the building envelope with their outside face on it, so on the east and west sides the outside face is on the side offset line (2 in inside the lot line) and the thickness builds inward.
extWall.wallModel: Every wall keeps the line it was drawn on, a thickness, and which side of that line it sits on (inside, centered or outside). Changing the thickness never moves the drawn line. Rebuilt exterior walls use the building envelope as their drawn line, sitting inside it.

envelope.label: Height and setback (R6, narrow street, qualifying affordable housing)
envelope.meaning: The street wall may rise to the max base height (min 30 ft, max 65 ft); any floor that rises above it must sit at least 15 ft back from the street line on a narrow street (10 ft on a wide street; reduced 1 ft per ft the street wall is set back, never under 7 ft); max building height 85 ft. Standard (non-qualifying) R6 on a narrow street is 45 ft base and 55 ft max height. Within 100 ft of a wide street the affordable limits are 65 ft base and 95 ft max.
envelope.thisBuilding: Floors 1-6 rise to 64'-11" at the street line; the 7th and 8th floors' street sides are 15'-0" back, at 105'-0" from the rear lot line.
envelope.dormers: A story above the base height may reach past the setback line as a dormer (ZR 23-413): its width along the street wall may be up to 60% of the street wall width at the base height, less 1% of the street wall for each foot above the base height (checked at the top of the story), or a flat 40% at any height. Dormers count as floor area.
envelope.dormerThisBuilding: 7th floor dormer 12'-4" wide x 6'-4" deep (78 SF) on the east half of the street setback, added to unit 7F; sized to use the last of the market-rate residential floor area (7,446 of 7,447 SF). The 7th floor top is 74'-11", so the limit is 50% of the 24'-8" street wall = 12'-4".

rearYard.label: Rear yard
rearYard.meaning: Every story above the ground floor keeps its rear wall (outside face) at least this far from the rear lot line. The ground floor may extend into the rear yard as a one-story permitted obstruction (check the district's limit, about 23 ft above curb for non-residential).
rearYard.rule: ZR 23-342: attached or semi-detached buildings on lots under 40 ft wide need 30 ft at every rear lot line. 20 ft applies only to detached and zero lot line buildings, or to lots 40 ft or wider (at or below 75 ft). The R6 20 ft modification in 23-723 is limited to Brooklyn Community District 12.
rearYard.thisBuilding: 25 ft wide attached lot: 30 ft. Floors 4-7 moved back to 30'-0" (2026-10-19). Project owner: the 1st and 2nd floors may fill the rear yard (obstructionStories 2).

balconies.label: Balconies (cantilevered outdoor space)
balconies.meaning: A terrace with no floor under it is a balcony. In yards, courts and other required open areas a balcony may project the lesser of 7 ft or one third of the open area's depth from the wall (the one-third limit does not apply in setback areas required by height and setback rules), cover at most 10% of a required open area, and the balconies on any story may total at most 50% of that wall's width. Unenclosed except parapets to 4 ft or railings to 4'-6" (at least 50% open above 4 ft); at least 13 ft above curb. In a rear yard, not within 5 ft of the rear lot line. Balconies at most 67% enclosed are not floor area.
balconies.thisBuilding: Rear balconies on floors 5-7 (5th projects 7'-6", over the 7 ft limit by 6"; owner says OK), 8th floor street balcony 7'-0" over the 7th floor terrace, 12'-4" of a 24'-8" wall (50%).

affordable.label: Residential affordable areas
affordable.meaning: Drawn inside the gross outline like a Residential area; counts as residential floor area and is tracked as affordable. When any are drawn, the market-rate residential check subtracts their total instead of the affordable unit zoning input.

facade.label: Façade (renderings)
facade.styles: frame: a limestone giant order over the street wall (below), the owner's choice; ribbon: a sculpted white GFRC skin (tried and set aside 10/19/2026, too busy); masonry: the punched-window brick base described in meaning

frame.meaning: Clean lines for a high-end boutique street wall. Limestone ashlar from the storefront head to parapetFt above the first setback floor, with pierFt piers at the lot lines and bays equal bays split by mullionFt stone mullions that run unbroken through each group of floors. Consecutive floors of the same class form a group: the commercial and amenity floors make a double-height base, the residential floors below the setback a single giant order; a bandFt stone band separates the groups. Glass sits glassDepthFt behind the stone face in slim bronze frames, each floor with a fixed and an operable lite and a bronze guard rail at 42 in; bronze spandrel panels sit spandrelDepthFt back at each slab inside a group. The parapet carries one bronze shadow line and a smooth stone coping. Nothing projects past the street line. Setback floors: storey-high glass and bronze.
frame.spandrelMeaning: Floor-line spandrels in a light champagne bronze, brighter than the window frames
frame.windowBoxMeaning: A slim bronze window box at the foot of each front bay on the floors inside a group (not the first floor of a group), planted with trailing greenery that falls 2-8 ft over the spandrel below

thinBrick.meaning: The frame (piers, mullions, bands, parapet) in long thin bricks (about 21 x 1.5 in face, Kolumba-like) laid vertically, a warm buff-to-honey blend with a slightly recessed joint; replaces the limestone so the street wall reads residential, not office. Coping stays smooth stone.

frame.partyMeaning: Lot-line walls (no openings) in a face brick toned between the neighbours (here #242's buff and the church's red), lightly weathered, not the street-wall stone

ribbon.meaning: One sculpted skin over the street wall from startFt above grade to parapetFt above the first setback floor. Each floor below the base height gets one long eye-shaped opening: half-width = half the façade - pierFt - |shift|, centred at half the façade + shift (shiftsFt, cycled floor by floor, so the openings' ends alternate and the bands swell and pinch), height = the floor height - 1 ft - 2 x bandMinFt, lens-shaped tips (superellipse endShape), its mid-line waving by waveFt and leaning by tiltFt across the opening, alternating floor by floor so the bands taper. Every edge rolls back over rollFt into a revealFt-deep reveal; glass and slim mullions sit behind. The skin's crown is on the street line (no projection over the street). Lot-line and rear walls get the same white finish with the ribbons as low relief; setback floors and terrace edges get rounded white bands.

facade.meaning: How a façade is generated from the floor outlines when the model has no façade design. Base (below envelope.baseFt): masonry with punched windows centred in bays of about bayFt, window width = bay - pierMinFt (at most windowMaxWFt), sill sillFt above the finished floor, head headBelowFt below the next floor, a precast sill, a bronze guard bar at 42 in and a soldier course at every slab. Commercial floors above grade: one wide opening per face (1'-7" brick piers), glazed as a curtain wall. Floors at or above the base height, and floors with no gross outline (an amenity room on a terrace level): storey-high glass in bronze frames on curtainBayFt mullions. Ground floor on the street: retail glass with a recessed residential entry and canopy at the core end. Lot-line walls: the same brick with no openings and the slab soldier course. Terrace edges over masonry: brick upstand and coping with glass above; elsewhere frameless glass.
facade.thisBuilding: Warm grey Roman brick (12 x 2 in courses) with dark bronze frames; floors 4-6 get three 6'-2" windows per 24'-8" face; floors 7-8 and the 3rd floor amenity room are glass and bronze

retail.meaning: Shop interiors seen through the storefront: plaster ceiling at the storefront head with small warm (about 3000 K) recessed downlights on a 5.5 ft grid, a light oak slatted back wall washed by a cove, polished concrete floor, a stone display table under glass globe pendants; the lobby in the same light and oak. No panel lights.

interiors.meaning: Every floor behind the street glass is furnished as a lived-in front room 20 ft deep: plaster ceiling with warm (3000 K) downlights on a 6 ft grid, an oak or plaster back wall with art and shelving, a linen sofa on a rug, a stone coffee table, a floor lamp, a potted tree by the window; commercial floors a long oak table under globe pendants. Glass IOR 1.45 and few sheers, so the rooms read from the street. No panel lights.

landscape.meaning: Every terrace, balcony and roof deck gets wood decking and planters with shrubs along its open edges; larger ones a dining set; the penthouse roof a pergola over a dining area at the street end, a fire pit and potted trees

facade.source: Design assumption for the renderings (scripts/render/render_scene.py), not a design; frame style chosen by the owner for clean lines, 10/19/2026 (a Zaha-like ribbon skin was tried first). Replace with the architect's façade when there is one

liveWorkTriplex.label: Commercial live/work triplex (cellar, 1st, 2nd)
liveWorkTriplex.rule: A three-story planted atrium at the rear, across the 30 ft wide rear 19'-6", from planting beds and trees on the cellar floor up to an operable glass roof on top of the 2nd floor. The 1st floor is open to below over the atrium. The 2nd floor over the atrium is a walkable glass floor (a walkway along the lot line and a 4 ft bridge) with openings between, so light and air reach the cellar. Kitchen and dining are on the cellar garden level. The 1st floor is an open studio and showroom with a gallery that runs to the garage. The garage has a glass overhead door on the street and a second glass overhead door inside, so it opens to the gallery. The 2nd floor has offices around the atrium and bedrooms on the street windows (atrium and lot-line windows are not legal windows for sleeping rooms).
liveWorkTriplex.floorArea: Openings in a floor (Open to below) are not floor area; the part inside the gross outline comes off. A glass floor is floor area.
codeChecks: Atrium: NYC BC 404 (smoke control, sprinklers) applies when an opening connects more than two stories; the cellar-1st-2nd atrium connects three.
Garage to live/work: the separation the Building Code requires (406) needs a rated door or fire shutter on the inside garage door, or the garage counted as part of the space.
Glass floor: rated for floor live load and walkable/slip-resistant; guards (42 in) at every edge of the 2nd-floor openings and at the 1st-floor atrium edge.
liveWorkTriplex.lotLineWindows: Cellar, 1st and 2nd floors (the #242 court is open down to its cellar, about 12 ft): lot-line windows on the west wall where it faces #242's court yard (44'-4" to 83'-8" from the rear), kept 6 in clear of the court's ends. They give daylight to the gallery, office 3 and the library, but they are not legal windows. They need protected (fire-rated) openings and, under the Building Code's fire separation rules, a recorded light-and-air easement from #242 so the court stays open. Cellar: four 6 ft windows, 3 ft sill and 9'-6" head, two in the live/work cellar past the stair and two in the community facility space.
liveWorkTriplex.rearLotLineWindows: 1st and 2nd floors: three 6 ft lot-line windows in the rear wall (on the rear lot line) onto the atrium, centered 5'-6", 15'-0" and 24'-6" from the west lot line. 1st floor sill 3 ft, head 11 ft; 2nd floor sill 2'-6", head 9 ft. Like all lot-line windows they need fire-protected glazing and a light-and-air easement, here from the lot behind; they are not legal windows.

recessedTerrace.label: Recessed rear terrace with a balcony beyond
recessedTerrace.source: ZR 12-10 floor area exclusion 9 (balconies and terraces); project owner 2026-10-22; tried on the 5th floor rear unit
recessedTerrace.rule: A terrace recessed into the rear of a unit is not floor area only if no more than 67% of its perimeter is enclosed (lot-line walls, including the neighbor's, count as enclosure; parapets up to 4 ft, railings up to 4'-6" and 50% open, and glass guards up to 10 ft and 90% transparent do not). Open on the rear side only, with walls on the other three sides: depth <= 0.515 x width (6'-7" at 12'-10"). A balcony may continue beyond it, up to 7'-0" from the rear wall and 50% of the rear wall width per story. Each is tested on its own (the conservative reading). Under a roofed portion, the open side needs an opening at least 40% of the floor-to-ceiling height.
recessedTerrace.thisBuilding: 5th floor rear (5R): 6'-7" x 12'-10" recessed terrace (84 SF, 66.95% enclosed) plus a 7'-0" x 12'-4" balcony, 13'-7" of outdoor depth in all.

siteInputs246South2nd.communityFacilityNote: R6 community facility FAR 4.8, confirmed by the project owner (2026-10-18). Community facility areas, floors and sellable areas are tracked separately; the total FAR still caps all uses together.
siteInputs246South2nd.neighbors: #242 (west, 6-story brick): rear wall 18.4 ft from our rear lot line; court yard on our west lot line 44.3-83.7 ft from the rear, 10.1 ft deep, with a 1-story piece at 83.7-93.1 ft. #248 (east): 1-story brick from 20 to 57.5 ft, 1-story church 57.5-113.7 ft. From Survey No. 6097 (A & B Engineering, 10/11/2015); heights estimated.
siteInputs246South2nd.unitMix: 4F affordable 1BR (858 SF), 4R/5R/6R 1BR (~725 SF), 5F/6F 2BR/2BA (858 SF), 7F studio + 370 SF terrace, 7R 1BR + terrace, PH full 8th floor 2BR/2BA (863 SF) + 435 SF terraces + 1,505 SF private roof. Units are drawn to the offering plan lines.
siteInputs246South2nd.hardCostBasis: Project owner, per gross SF; confirm whether it is per gross above grade or including the cellar
siteInputs246South2nd.affordableTenure: For sale (affordable homeownership), valued at affordable pricing, not market comps
siteInputs246South2nd.orientation: Plan top edge (y = 0) is the west lot line, bottom edge is the east lot line, right edge is South 2nd Street

rearUnitBathCloset.source: user layout on the 6th floor rear unit, copied to floors 4, 5, 7 (2026-10-19)
rearUnitBathCloset.rule: Behind the bedroom: a linen closet (about 2 ft 10 in deep) opening to the bedroom with a 3 ft slider, then the bath (about 5 ft 6 in x 7 ft 6 in) with the tub across the far (east) end, the WC and vanity along the mech-closet wall, a 2 ft 6 in door from the foyer, and a 2 ft 4 in slider between the closet and the bath. The stacked W/D goes in the mechanical closet instead of a separate laundry room.

interiors.label: Interior design package (finishes, FF&E, interior renderings)
interiors.market: Condominium for sale. Goal: record pricing for a boutique (non-waterfront) Williamsburg building.
interiors.pricingContext: Williamsburg record: One Domino Square penthouse, $3,313/SF (Feb 2026, waterfront, Two Trees); previous record $3,046/SF, same building (2025). Proforma base $1,750-$1,900/SF. Set the target from the comps pull, not from this note.
interiors.inspiration: Soho Home (Soho House's furniture line): warm, layered, club-like rooms that look collected over time, not staged. Use as a reference only: no Soho House / Soho Home names or marks in the marketing. Individual Soho Home pieces may be specified in the FF&E schedule.

palette.floors: Wide-plank European white oak, fumed or smoked oil finish, laid in herringbone in living/dining (stand-in for chevron until a chevron pattern is modelled); straight plank in bedrooms
palette.walls: Lime plaster or limewash in warm neutrals; one saturated accent per unit (bottle green, oxblood, ochre or ink) on a den, powder room or millwork
palette.metals: Unlacquered brass (left to patinate) for plumbing fittings and hardware; aged bronze for window and door frames
palette.stone: Kitchens: full-height book-matched slab backsplash and waterfall island in a characterful marble (Calacatta Viola or Arabescato class). Baths: honed marble floors with handmade zellige or glazed terracotta walls
palette.millwork: Reeded or fluted oak and painted panelled cabinetry with inset doors; walnut or dark-stained oak in dens and bars
palette.textiles: Velvet, boucle, linen, leather; cane and rattan accents; vintage-style hand-knotted rugs
palette.lighting: 2700 K, dimmable, layered: sconces, picture lights, table and floor lamps, under-shelf light; minimal recessed downlights, never a grid

tiers.rule: Finish level follows the unit, not the floor. Signature: PH and the townhouse (custom millwork, slab stone, specialist plaster). Residence: all other market units (same materials, standard millwork). Affordable: the same finish package as Residence unless the affordable housing agency allows otherwise (confirm with HPD).
tiers.budget: Interior $/SF per tier set from the priced FF&E schedule; feeds the proforma

heroViews: PH living/kitchen toward the South 2nd windows
renderings.engine: Blender Cycles from the same model (scripts/render), interiors built from the drawn units, rooms, openings and fixtures; views out of the windows from the Google 3D Tiles context
renderings.hardware: RTX 2060 with 4 GB VRAM: cap textures at 2K for drafts; finals may need CPU rendering or a rented GPU
renderings.disclosure: Label renderings as artist's renderings; finishes shown must match the offering plan specification (confirm with the offering plan attorney).

package: FF&E, plumbing, hardware, appliance, lighting and finish schedules (.xlsx)
interiors.format: HTML -> PDF in the OM's style, plus a shareable web version; schedules in .xlsx

furniture.decided: 2026-10-21, project owner: model every piece in-house rather than buying 3D models
furniture.rule: Each FF&E piece is built in code (scripts/render/interior_lib.py) at the size its reference product publishes, so a renamed or resized product only changes numbers. Pieces are our own drawings in the reference's spirit, not replicas. CC0 Poly Haven scans supply surface detail (fabric, wood, plaster); stone, brass, cane and velvet are procedural.
furniture.references: Soho Home US product pages (checked 2026-10-21): Mossley sofa 92x39x30, Sydney cane armchair 39x33x34, Ewan leather armchair 32x36x29, Ramsey travertine coffee table 55.1x31.5x15, Cavern side table 20x20x18, Elliot travertine dining table 87x39x29, Molina cane dining chair 20x23x31, Wardell counter stool 15x15x25, Penny pendant 28 dia, Oregan wall light 5.3x5.9x8, Reno table lamp 14x14x24, Calabria floor lamp 15x15x66 (inches)

phGreatRoom.decided: 2026-10-21, project owner (chose 'island is the dining' over a separate table)
phGreatRoom.rule: In a great room under about 12 x 15 ft, the island is the dining: no separate table. Kitchen run on the inside (lot line) wall, a 6 x 3 ft island with 12 in overhang and three counter stools, a 3'-3" aisle between run and island, and the living group at the street windows with the path to the balcony slider kept clear.
phGreatRoom.thisBuilding: PH (8th floor): run 92'-4 1/2" to 101'-3" on the west wall (carried past the drawn counter so the 6 ft lot line window is centred over it); panelled refrigerator column at the left end; sink under the window; island 93'-3" to 99'-3" x 6'-3" to 9'-3" with a flush induction cooktop on the kitchen side; 76 in velvet sofa backed to the street wall under the 3 ft window, travertine coffee table, cane lounge chair, side table and lamp by the slider, money tree in the corner.
phGreatRoom.flag: The room is small for record pricing (about 11'-7" x 14'-7" plus the foyer, with the open stair to the roof beside it). A larger great room would need a plan change.

kitchen.rule: Painted inset Shaker cabinetry in the unit's accent colour (bottle green in the PH) with unlacquered brass pulls; 1 1/4 in book-matched marble counters, a full-height slab backsplash and a waterfall island; fluted (reeded) oak island base; panelled refrigerator; fireclay undermount sink with a brass bridge faucet; flush induction cooktop in the island (no hood over a window).
kitchen.windowOverCounter: A window over a counter has its sill at 3'-6" (counter at 36 in plus a 6 in stone ledge), not the 2'-6" default.
kitchen.lighting: Two bubbled-glass globe pendants on brass rods over the island, sconces flanking the street window, lamps rather than recessed downlights.
